title: Registries: Docker Hub, GHCR, ECR, GCR, ACR and a private registry

videos.script: Every image so far was pulled from somewhere, and that somewhere has a name. {{name}} An image's name says which server to ask, which repository, and which version. Most of it is usually left out, and Docker fills it in. {{tag}} A tag is a label that can move. A digest is the content's own hash, and it cannot. {{registry}} Then Ana runs a registry of her own, with a password, and pushes shelf to it. The first push is refused. The login works, and leaves the password in a file anyone can decode. {{digest}} She pulls the image back by its digest, and gets exactly the bytes she pushed. {{hosted}} Last, the hosted registries. They all speak the same protocol. What differs is how you log in.
